summary: Module 1 REFLECT (AI-Augmented Engineering). The role shift is the module's core: I am no longer a typist, I am a reviewer/decider who decomposes, delegates, reviews, and ships -- and the AI output becomes MY code on acceptance. The 80/20 split means the 20% review pass is where engineering skill lives; skipping it ships the 80% prototype. Key lessons internalized: (1) preparation before the first prompt -- map the real data model, routing, and error patterns so the Capable Intern does not invent assumptions; verified against this fork (User/Link/ClickEvent, no Team tables). (2) Trust-but-verify discipline -- 6/6 spot-checks matched, but the negative claim (no Team tables) is the pattern most worth verifying; 1-2 spot-checks per summary biased toward claims that change prompt design. (3) Failure-mode triage: the wrong-claim card was a context/pattern failure (fixable with a better prompt), not hallucination and not ambiguous code -- but negative structural claims get a command check regardless because the cost of a wrong 'no code exists' conclusion is total. (4) Task-by-task delegation (decision B): error-discovery-cost asymmetry favors small diffs; one flawed foundation assumption replicating through 8 features costs far more than 8 review checkpoints. The entire discipline reduces to: the AI generates, I decide -- and I decide from evidence, not confidence.
evidence: Wrong-claim card disproved with commands; fix-record.md failure-mode analysis
